title_en: Answers on the science of legal theory
body_ar:
رد خبر الآحاد في القرآن:

هل صحيح ما يقال أيضا من أن الصحابة رضوان الله عليهم قد كرسوا مبدأ رد خبر الآحاد هذا حين ردوا روايات آحاد الصحابة الثابتة فلم يثبتوا بها القراءة القرآنية وذلك كقراءة عشر رضعات معلومات وكقراءة فاقطعوا أيمانهما؟

الجواب: لا، هذا أيضا ليس من رد خبر الآحاد، فقد أثبت الصحابة أن القرآن لا بد أن يكون متواترا فلا يمكن أن يروى بخبر الآحاد فهو يختلف عن أخبار الآحاد، أخبار الآحاد لا تكون في القرآن إنما تكون في السنة فقط، ولهذا فلم يقبل الصحابة من القرآن ما رواه آحاد قلائل إلا آية واحدة وجدوها مكتوبة ولم يجدوا من يحفظها إلا خزيمة بن ثابت ولكن رسول الله (ص) جعل شهادته بشهادة رجلين، وهي قوله تعالى: {لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم عزيز عليه ما عنتم حريص عليكم بالمؤمنين رؤوف رحيم} ولم يترددوا أن هذا من كلام الله وأنه قد نزل على الرسول(ص)، بل قد سمعه كثير منهم وإنما ترددوا هل نسخت في العرضة الأخيرة أم لا؟ فأخبرهم خزيمة أنه سمعها من رسول الله (ص) في آخر قراءته لسورة التوبة فأثبتوها فيها، لأنهم علموا أن شهادته بشهادة رجلين.

*- حجية خبر الآحاد:

هل ينطبق هذا علينا نحن معاشر المسلمين إذ نعمل بأحاديث الآحاد التي لا تفيد إلا الظن مضمون الآية الكريمة: {إن نظن إلا ظنا وما نحن بمستيقنين}؟
body_en:
The rejection of the singly transmitted report in the Qur'an:

Is what is also said correct, namely that the Companions, may God be pleased with them, entrenched this principle of rejecting the singly transmitted report when they rejected established singly transmitted narrations of Companions and so did not establish a Qur'anic reading by them — as with the reading "ten known sucklings", and the reading "so cut off their right hands"?

The answer: No. This too is not a case of rejecting the singly transmitted report. The Companions established that the Qur'an must be mass-transmitted, so that it cannot be narrated by a singly transmitted report: it differs from the singly transmitted reports. Singly transmitted reports do not occur in the Qur'an; they occur in the sunnah only. For this reason the Companions did not accept as Qur'an anything narrated by a few individuals — except one verse, which they found written down and for which they found no one who had memorised it but Khuzaymah ibn Thabit; but the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, had made his testimony equal to the testimony of two men. It is God Most High's words: {There has come to you a messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is that you should suffer; he is deeply concerned for you, and to the believers kind and merciful} (Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:128). They did not doubt that this is the speech of God and that it had been sent down upon the Messenger, upon whom be peace — indeed many of them had heard it. They doubted only whether it had been abrogated in the final review or not. Khuzaymah informed them that he had heard it from the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, in his last recitation of Sūrat al-Tawbah, so they established it in it, because they knew that his testimony was equal to the testimony of two men.

*- The probative force of the singly transmitted report:

Does this apply to us, the community of Muslims, since we act upon singly transmitted hadiths which yield nothing but probability — the substance of the noble verse: {We only conjecture, and we are not certain}?

flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The second question is a challenge to the probative force of singly transmitted hadith, put in the form of a verse in which disbelievers say they have only conjecture. Published with no answer beneath it, the page leaves that challenge standing as though the Sheikh had no reply — which is the opposite of what a legal theory course would conclude. The full material is behind the .docx download in source_download_link.

flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW REQUESTED — this flag concerns publication, not the translation, which is faithful. The exchange turns on variant readings that are not in the ʿUthmanic codex and on the abrogation of Qur'anic wording in the final review. This is entirely standard matter in Arabic works of legal theory and hadith, and the Sheikh's answer is itself a defence of the Qur'an's mass transmission. But the subject is one that is routinely quoted out of context in English-language polemic, and the page as published gives the questioner's framing without the Sheikh's full treatment, because the answer to the second question is missing. Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office should decide whether this page is published at all before the full text is recovered. The translator's view, recorded for the file, is that it should not be.

flags.note: Minor. This page divides its two entries with '*-' where the comparable compilations at ids 639 and 640 use a row of hyphens. The inconsistency is the source's and is preserved in both body_ar and body_en. A site-wide rendering decision is needed for these dividers.

translator_notes: TYPING DECISION. The source presents this page as 'answers' (ajwibah) to questions put to the Sheikh, in the same question-and-answer form as the written fatwas. It is typed 'article' rather than 'fatwa' because it contains no ruling on an act: the glossary fixes fatwā as 'a considered legal opinion', and this page is explanatory. The site must not display it as a fatwa, or readers will take its contents for rulings.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

The CMS holds the tapes out of order across ids 649–652 and the tape numbers in the titles do not run with the ids; the series should be ordered by the tape number in the title, not by id, and tape two does not appear anywhere in the range 601–652.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off and the full material is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
'Singly transmitted' renders āḥād and 'mass-transmitted' renders mutawātir, per the glossary. The whole exchange turns on the distinction and the two must never be blurred.

'The final review' renders al-ʿarḍah al-akhīrah, the last occasion on which the Prophet is reported to have gone through the Qur'an with Gabriel; wording abrogated at that point did not enter the codex.
'Entrenched' renders karrasū — established as a settled principle.

The verse at Sūrat al-Jāthiyah 45:32 is spoken in the Qur'an by those who deny the Resurrection; the questioner is using it as a description of acting on probability, not endorsing the speakers. The English keeps it as a quotation so that the frame is visible.
The verse references have been supplied per house style; the source gives the verse texts alone.
Unusually for this range, the answer is introduced by an explicit 'al-jawāb:' ('the answer:'), so the standing note about the elliptical particle 'anna does not apply to this record.
